key_insight: The paper argues that making biological data truly "AI-ready" is not just a technical cleanup task—it requires answering four foundational questions about data meaning, structure, quality, and usability. The central message is that AI performance in biology depends on how well data are prepared to match biological complexity and model needs.
problem_solved: It addresses the lack of a clear framework for defining what "AI-ready" means for biological data. Researchers and practitioners need guidance on how to evaluate whether biological datasets are suitable for reliable machine learning and AI analysis.
method: Frames the AI-readiness challenge around four guiding questions for biological data.
Uses these questions to organize practical criteria for data quality, representation, and downstream model use.
Provides a conceptual model rather than a new algorithm, aimed at standardizing thinking about biological data preparation.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this helps clarify how to assess and improve biological datasets before modeling, reducing avoidable errors and bias. It supports better model performance, interpretability, and reproducibility in biology-focused AI work.
visual_elements: A central four-part question wheel showing the paper’s framework
A pipeline diagram from raw biological data to AI-ready data to model output
An icon-based checklist for data quality, structure, annotation, and usability
A comparison graphic showing 'raw data' vs 'AI-ready data'
paper_title: Four questions for AI-ready biological data
